core_obligations: Chain of bijections (proof lines 4611-4624): for an arbitrary sheaf the author computes the morphism set out of the sheafification of the inverse image of the sheafified presheaf and rewrites it successively through the adjunctions with the two functors on sheaves and presheaves attached to the cocontinuous functor, obtaining the morphism set out of the sheafification of the inverse image of the original presheaf.
Conclusion (proof line 4625): the two sheaves represent the same functor, so they agree by the Yoneda lemma.
proof_roadmap: Compare the functors represented by the two sheaves on an arbitrary sheaf.
Rewrite the morphism sets through the adjunctions attached to the cocontinuous functor.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that sheafifying the inverse image of a presheaf gives the same sheaf as sheafifying the inverse image of its sheafification (statement lines 4603-4608). The proof is a complete computation: the author compares the functors represented by the two sheaves and rewrites the morphism sets through the adjunctions between the functors on sheaves and presheaves attached to the cocontinuous functor (proof lines 4611-4624), concluding by the Yoneda lemma (proof line 4625). The non-formal content is the chain of adjunction rewritings. The claim is H1: a written-out computation with each input named.
